nodes.summary: The alpha sequence $U_n=\alpha_b(n)$ satisfies $U_0=0$, $U_1=1$, $U_{n+2}=bU_{n+1}-U_n$. It grows for $b\ge2$, its matrix powers have determinant one, and it is congruent in its parameter, with $\alpha_2(n)=n$.
nodes.title: The alpha and power formulas

nodes.summary: The compiler writes its conditions as formulas over integer polynomials with fresh natural witnesses: equality is a difference, conjunction a sum of squares, disjunction a product, and strict inequality, divisibility, congruence and oddness are single equations with fresh witnesses.
nodes.title: Natural constructions and the power interface

nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal N$ be the five-input natural precision circuit, with variable count $1{,}305{,}811$ and polynomial $[\![\mathcal N]\!]\in\mathbb Z[X_0,\dots,X_{1305810}]$ (call nodes denoting literal substitution into the power template). For every $c\in\mathbb N^5$, where $\operatorname{accepts}$ is the precision relation: with $(n,\kappa,a,l,j)$ the signed decoding of $c$, the early tests $n\notin\mathcal C$,…
nodes.title: Semantics of the natural precision polynomial

nodes.summary: A primitive program with $m$ instructions over $r$ registers is compiled by packing a run of length $q$ into base-$B$ integers, with $K=2^c$, $B=4K>m$, $T=B^q$, $F_q=1+B+\dots+B^q$ and $D=(K-1)F_q$, every input being below $K$.
nodes.title: The packed-history compiler

nodes.summary: The five natural inputs of the precision computation are signed encodings, decoded in the fixed order $(n,\kappa,a,l,j)$.
nodes.title: The exact precision computation

nodes.summary: Register machines have increment, decrement-or-branch and halt instructions. A primitive program halts only at its last instruction; it accepts when it halts with every register zero.
nodes.title: Programs, lowering and the wrapper

nodes.summary: Programs are numbered by $e+1=2^w(2D+1)$, with four base-$2^w$ digits of $D$ per state; decoding is total. A valid primitive program has a code whose machine halts exactly when the program does.
